title: Task result request
description: POST /api/v1/tasks/<id>/result (FR-3.2, P3-S04). The task's final result, sent once the agent has recorded it as finished in its ledger and retried until accepted (P3-A02). Sending the same result again is accepted and changes nothing (duplicate: true); a different result for a task that already has one is refused with 409 task_conflict and logged. The host is the credential's host, never a field in the body; a task of another host, or an unknown id, is 404 not_found.

schema_version.description: Payload schema version. This directory is version 1.

report_id.description: UUIDv4, generated once per result and reused on every retry of it.

outcome.description: succeeded: the task ran and did what it says. failed: it ran, or may have run, and did not succeed (reason says why). timed_out: it ran over its deadline and the agent terminated it. cancelled: the agent stopped an interruptible task the operator cancelled. refused: the agent ran nothing (reason says why; AC-3.1).

reason.description: Why the task failed or was refused: required for those outcomes, and null or absent for the others. failed: nonzero_exit, interrupted (the agent stopped mid-task, or found a started task without a result when it started again), lock_timeout (the package manager's lock stayed held), agent_error, or not_run (the agent holds the task in its ledger but never ran it, because the server never answered its start with run: true; it sends this when the server delivers that id again, so the task is closed instead of waiting for its expiry; P3-S05). refused: unknown_type, invalid_params, not_supported, not_enabled_locally, not_allowed_locally, or protected_service.

exit_status.description: The task's process exit status, 0 to 255, or null when there is none (refused, killed by a signal, or never started).

started_at.description: When the task started (agent clock), RFC 3339 UTC; null when it never started (refused). Stored apart from the server's own times.

finished_at.description: When the task finished, or was refused (agent clock), RFC 3339 UTC. Stored apart from the server's own times.

details.description: Structured facts about the result, each optional. The server stores those it knows and ignores others.

reboot_required.description: apply_package_updates: the VM needs a reboot to finish the updates (DEC-16). The agent never reboots.

services_needing_restart.description: apply_package_updates: services still running old code after the updates, each once. The agent never restarts them (DEC-16).

packages_upgraded.description: apply_package_updates: how many installed packages have a new version after the upgrade, from dpkg's database before and after. Absent when either listing could not be read, or the agent restarted during the upgrade (the next package report shows the versions).

packages_held_back.description: apply_package_updates: packages with a newer version available that the upgrade left as they were (on hold, or the upgrade would need a new package or a removal), each once, sorted. Absent when not known.

unit_active.description: restart_service: whether the unit was active after the restart.

reports_sent.description: refresh_reports: the report types sent and accepted, each once.

output.description: The task's captured output (stdout and stderr), as text; null or empty when there is none. At most 131072 characters: the agent truncates first and says so in output_truncated. The server keeps up to its own limit (64 KiB), cutting the middle out with a marker line when it is longer, replaces invalid UTF-8, removes control characters other than tab and newline (and terminal escape sequences), and stores it as inert text.

output_truncated.description: True when the agent cut the output down before sending it.
